title: In 2 Chronicles 16 What Are The Consequences Of Rejecting Gods Guidance And Correction In Our Lives
paragraphs: Introduction

2 Chronicles 16 tells the story of King Asa, a ruler of Judah who began his reign well—trusting God and seeking His guidance. However, in his later years, Asa made choices that reflected self-reliance and a rejection of God's correction. This chapter offers profound lessons on the consequences of rejecting God's guidance and correction in our lives.
Background: King Asa’s Early Faithfulness
Earlier in Asa's reign, he sought the Lord in times of trouble and experienced remarkable deliverance (2 Chronicles 14:9-13 ASV). God's blessing was evident while Asa depended on Him.
Asa’s Turning Point: Trusting in Human Wisdom
In 2 Chronicles 16, Asa faces a new threat from Baasha, king of Israel. Rather than seeking the Lord, Asa turns to an alliance with Ben-hadad, king of Syria:

Then Asa brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of Jehovah and of the king’s house, and sent to Ben-hadad king of Syria... saying, There is a league between me and thee... come, break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me. - 2 Chronicles 16:2-3 ASV
This action marks a shift from faith in God to reliance on human strategy.
God’s Rebuke Through Hanani the Seer
God sends Hanani the seer to confront Asa’s mistake:
Because thou hast relied on the king of Syria, and hast not relied on Jehovah thy God, therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of thy hand. - 2 Chronicles 16:7 ASV
Hanani reminds Asa of God's past faithfulness and challenges his lack of trust.
The Principle of Divine Guidance
God desires His people to seek Him in every circumstance:
For the eyes of Jehovah run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to show himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. - 2 Chronicles 16:9 ASV
Rejecting God's guidance is seen as folly and leads to negative consequences.
Consequences of Rejecting God’s Guidance and Correction

Loss of Peace: Hanani declares, “From henceforth thou shalt have wars” (2 Chronicles 16:9 ASV). Asa's decision led to ongoing conflict rather than peace—highlighting that rejecting God's way results in turmoil.
Spiritual Hardness: Instead of repenting, Asa becomes angry and imprisons Hanani:
Then Asa was wroth with the seer, and put him in the prison house; for he was in a rage with him because of this thing. - 2 Chronicles 16:10 ASV
Rejecting correction often leads to a hardened heart and further sin.

Physical and Spiritual Decline: Later, Asa becomes diseased in his feet, yet even then he “sought not to Jehovah, but to the physicians” (2 Chronicles 16:12 ASV). Persistent rejection of God’s help can result in both spiritual and physical suffering.
New Testament Application
The New Testament warns believers of the dangers of hardening our hearts when God speaks:
Today if ye shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts. - Hebrews 3:15 ASV
God graciously corrects us for our good (Hebrews 12:5-11 ASV), and we are called to respond in humility and faith.
Conclusion: The Call to Humble Trust

Asa’s story is a sober warning against relying on our own wisdom and rejecting God’s correction. God’s guidance is always rooted in His love and faithfulness. The way of blessing, peace, and spiritual vitality is to trust in the Lord with all our hearts:
Trust in Jehovah with all thy heart, And lean not upon thine own understanding: In all thy ways acknowledge him, And he will direct thy paths. - Proverbs 3:5-6 ASV
